planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; Nijinsky's tightly packed ball blooms benefit from a single stake on taller plants.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring. Introduced in Britain in 1970, Nijinsky forms perfectly spherical, fully double ball blooms in rich purple, roughly 3.5 inches across, held on strong upright stems. The dense, ray-like arrangement of incurved florets makes it a reliable, long-lasting cut flower from midsummer through fall. Feed and water consistently through the growing season, then lift and store tubers after the foliage is blackened by frost in all but the mildest climates.

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; stake early, since Shiloh Noelle's dinnerplate blooms are heavy on tall stems.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed, staking at planting time to support the tall stems. Shiloh Noelle produces huge, fully double dinnerplate blooms 8-10 inches across in soft lavender, blush, and cream tones with a deeper rose-toned center, giving each flower a watercolor-like blend of color. The long, sturdy stems make it an excellent cut flower, and it blooms steadily from midseason through frost. Feed monthly for best size and lift tubers for winter storage once frost blackens the foliage.

common_name: Gitts Attention Dahlia (White Informal Decorative Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; Gitts Attention blooms early and consistently, making it a favorite for cutting gardens.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring. Bred by Gitts and introduced around 2000, this informal decorative dahlia produces exceptionally full white blooms 4-6 inches across with petals that are delicately fringed at the tips. It flowers early and prolifically from midsummer into fall, and its long vase life has made it a standout white variety for cut-flower growers. Feed regularly through the season and lift tubers for winter storage once frost blackens the foliage.

common_name: Mystic Dreamer Dahlia (Pink and White Striped Single Dahlia with Black Foliage)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; Mystic Dreamer's sturdy, well-branched habit rarely needs staking.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring. Bred by New Zealand dahlia breeder Keith Hammett as part of the Mystic series, this cultivar pairs filigreed, deep mahogany-to-black foliage with single pink-and-white striped flowers surrounding a dark central disc. It blooms continuously from summer through autumn on a compact, well-branched plant that is useful in containers, borders, and mixed beds. The dark foliage holds its color best with consistent moisture and full sun.

common_name: Mystic Enchantment Dahlia (Fire-Engine Red Single Dahlia with Black Foliage)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; Mystic Enchantment's dark mahogany foliage colors best in full sun.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring. Another member of Keith Hammett's Mystic series, patented as USPP23332, Mystic Enchantment bears bright fire-engine red single flowers with a dark central disc over the same filigreed, near-black foliage that defines the series. It blooms heavily from summer into fall on a compact, well-branched plant that rarely needs staking. The glowing flower color and dark leaves pair well with silver or chartreuse companions in containers and borders.

common_name: Mystic Spirit Dahlia (Apricot-Peach Single Dahlia with Black Foliage)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; Mystic Spirit's Mystic-series foliage is among the darkest of any dahlia.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring. A patented selection from Keith Hammett's Mystic series, Mystic Spirit carries pale apricot single flowers with blush-peach overtones and a contrasting deep burgundy disc, set against the series' signature mahogany-black foliage. It blooms from June until October on an upright, well-branched plant that works equally well in containers or mixed borders. Consistent moisture and full sun keep both the foliage color and flower production strong.

common_name: Happy Single First Love Dahlia (Peach-Pink Single Patio Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed, or set out started plants; this compact Happy Single series member needs no staking.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring, or set out started plants after frost danger passes. Happy Single First Love bears single, open-faced flowers blending peach-pink and yellow around a narrow red ring and dark brown disc, held above dark bronze foliage. The broad, flat petals give easy access to nectar and pollen, making it a strong draw for bees and butterflies. Its compact, self-supporting habit blooms from midsummer until frost and suits containers, patios, and small-space borders without staking.

common_name: Hamari Girl Dahlia (Pink Large Decorative Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; stake at planting time to support Hamari Girl's large, heavy blooms.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed, staking early to carry the weight of the large blooms. Raised in Britain in 1960 as part of the well-known Hamari series alongside siblings like Hamari Gold and Hamari Bride, Hamari Girl produces fully double decorative flowers in rich pink that can open 8-10 inches across on a vigorous, bushy plant with dark green, serrated foliage. It flowers from midsummer into fall and is a long-standing favorite on the British show bench. Feed regularly through the growing season and lift tubers for winter storage once frost blackens the foliage.

common_name: Camano Sitka Dahlia (Lemon Yellow to Flamingo Pink Incurved Cactus Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; stake Camano Sitka's tall stems at planting time.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring, staking tall stems early. Hybridized by Richard and Susan Ambrose of Camano Island and introduced around 2000, Camano Sitka is an incurved cactus dahlia whose narrow, recurved petals open golden yellow at the base and fade outward to flamingo pink, creating a soft two-tone blend across each 6-8 inch bloom. The tall, vigorous plant flowers from midsummer through fall and makes a striking, long-lasting cut flower. Feed regularly through the season and lift tubers for winter storage once frost blackens the foliage.

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; Alpen Cherub's vigorous, upright habit holds up well without heavy staking.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring. Introduced in 1987 from Bill McClaren's Alpen Gardens breeding program, Alpen Cherub is a collarette dahlia with pure white outer ray florets, a cheerful yellow center, and a smaller inner collar of white florets, each bloom 4-5 inches across. The vigorous, upright, bushy plant flowers freely from midsummer into fall and is a good pollinator plant thanks to its open center. Feed regularly through the season and lift tubers for winter storage once frost blackens the foliage.

common_name: Wizard of Oz Dahlia (Pink Ball Dahlia with Dark Purple Stems)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed; Wizard of Oz's stocky, manageable habit needs little staking.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring. Wizard of Oz is a ball dahlia with tightly packed, fully double pink flowers deepening to a richer pink center, each about 2-3 inches across and carried on distinctive dark purple stems above glossy deep green foliage. The strong, stocky growth habit keeps this cultivar compact and tidy without heavy staking, and it blooms steadily from midsummer into fall. Feed regularly through the season and lift tubers for winter storage once frost blackens the foliage.
